items.title: #NSTviral: SUV driver criticised after tailgating ambulance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An SUV driver has drawn widespread criticism after being seen tailgating an ambulance, prompting calls for action by the Road Transport Department. The driver also had the vehicle's hazard lights switched on while closely following the ambulance. Another user, Chek Fizie, tagged the authorities in the comments and said: "Road Transport Department, please revoke their licence."

items.title: No distance too great: Woman returns home to vote
items.summary: The 67-year-old flew home from Australia specifically to cast her ballot in the Negri Sembilan election for the Chennah state seat. Speaking to reporters, Lim said returning to vote was a responsibility she could not ignore. Although she now lives in Australia, Lim said Chennah remains her hometown.

items.title: 'I always feared this day would come,' says husband
items.summary: KUALA NERUS: A man whose pregnant wife and teenage son were injured in a crash involving a motorcyclist believed to be attending the RXZ Members 8.0 gathering said he had always feared for her safety whenever she left home. Talhah Mahmud, 61, said his wife, Syafirah Salim, 36, who is seven months pregnant with their third child, and their eldest son, Ahmad Asyraf, 13, were on their way from their home in Kampung Tanjung Sabtu to Batu Enam market to buy daily necessities when the crash occurred at the Jalan Buluh Gading four-way junction at 11.50am yesterday. "Whenever my heavily pregnant wife went out, I could never shake the feeling that something might happen.

items.title: Voting begins in Negeri Sembilan: A decisive day for 859,760 voters
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — Voters in Negeri Sembilan will fulfill their democratic rights and civic duty today in the 16th State Election (PRN) to elect their new people’s representatives. A total of 36 State Legislative Assembly (DUN) seats are being contested in this state election, involving 103 candidates. In this state election, 22 state seats face three-cornered fights, another 11 seats feature straight fights, and two seats each witness four-cornered and five-cornered contests.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polling opens across 401 centres in battle for 36 seats
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 1 — A total of 401 polling centres involving 1,668 streams for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election opened simultaneously at 8am today, with 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, eligible to cast their ballots in the contest for the 36 state seats. The 16th Negeri Sembilan state election sees 103 candidates, with Pakatan Harapan (PH) contesting all 36 seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 25, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) with 24, Perikatan Nasional (PN) with 11, and four independent candidates. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Spain says almost all migrants have returned to Morocco from Ceuta
items.summary: MADRID, (Spain): Almost all of the migrants who entered Ceuta have returned to Morocco, the Spanish foreign minister announced Friday, saying "enough of the deliberate misinformation." Enough of the deliberate misinformation." Spanish news agency EFE reported earlier that hundreds of migrants were heading toward the border Friday afternoon to return to Morocco, citing a repatriation agreement between Spain and Morocco as well as the lack of open shops, supermarkets and restaurants in Ceuta to meet basic needs.

items.title: MBSB commits RM4bil to Malaysia's high-growth industries
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: MBSB Bank is ramping up its support for Malaysia's high-growth, high-value (HGHV) industries, committing RM4 billion across four strategic sectors as it positions itself to play a larger role in financing the country's industrial transformation. The financing initiative is part of MBSB's strategy to diversify beyond its traditional strength in property financing by supporting companies operating in advanced manufacturing and technology-driven industries. Kamaruzaman said the bank's financing focus extends beyond the four priority sectors to companies involved in electrical and electronics, semiconductors, digital technology, artificial intelligence and green technology.

items.title: N9 polls: All 401 polling centres opened at 8am
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A total of 401 polling centres involving 1,668 streams for the 16th Negri Sembilan state election opened simultaneously at 8am today, with 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, eligible to cast their ballots for the 36 state seats. The 16th Negri Sembilan state election sees 103 candidates, with Pakatan Harapan (PH) contesting all 36 seats, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 25, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) with 24, Perikatan Nasional (PN) with 11 and four independent candidates. For the latest updates on the 16th Negri Sembilan state election, visit [https://prn.bernama.com/n9](https://prn.bernama.com/n9).

items.title: Govt wants EV charging network to keep pace with adoption [WATCH]
items.summary: TANJUNG MALIM: Malaysia must accelerate the rollout of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure while ensuring foreign automakers help develop the country's automotive ecosystem, the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry said. Johari said the ministry is targeting 30,000 public EV chargers nationwide, although no timeline has been set. Malaysia currently has about 1,000 public charging stations.

items.title: Reservoir Link eyes bigger role in liberalised gas market [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Reservoir Link Energy Bhd is positioning itself to capitalise on Malaysia's liberalised gas market after becoming one of the few listed companies to hold both a gas shipping licence and a liquefied natural gas (LNG) import licence, allowing it to participate across the gas value chain. Reservoir Link executive director Thien Chiet Chai said the dual licences gave the company an edge over listed peers that only hold a gas shipping licence. "A gas shipping licence enables the delivery of gas through the existing distribution network, which generally serves industrial customers.

items.title: Lessons from Japan's debt burden
items.summary: Japan today carries public debt exceeding 230 per cent of GDP—the highest among advanced economies. The return of inflation after 2022 has fundamentally altered the environment that allowed Japan to sustain exceptionally high public debt at exceptionally low borrowing costs. Japan Is Not Greece Any discussion of Japan's debt must begin by recognising that Japan is fundamentally different from previous sovereign debt crises.

items.title: Uniting people through football
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mosque communities, young footballers and Malaysians from diverse backgrounds will come together for the inaugural Federal Territory Islamic Religious Council's (MAIWP) 2026 Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Football Championship Cup next month. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the championship aimed to promote unity, patriotism, brotherhood and healthy living while strengthening the role of mosques within local communities. The tournament will feature 32 teams representing various mosques nationwide, with each state Islamic religious department sending two teams, and 10 teams representing mosques in the federal territories.

items.title: Alphabet rolls back AI image generation in Google Earth over policy violations
items.summary: MEXICO CITY: Alphabet's Google said on Friday it was rolling back an AI image-generation feature it had introduced in Google Earth just a day earlier, after users shared images that appeared to violate the company's policies. The feature, powered by Google's Nano Banana 2 AI model, had allowed users to generate photorealistic images based on Google Earth's satellite, aerial and 3D imagery by typing a text prompt for any location around the globe. Google did not specify what types of images violated its policies.

items.title: Fire breaks out at Red Square church in Moscow
items.summary: MOSCCOW: A fire broke out early Saturday at the St Basil's Cathedral in Moscow but was contained, TASS news agency said, quoting operational services. Around 10 fire engines were deployed to the scene. The fire is currently contained," the agency's source said.

items.title: Cubs spotted in Malaysia's first tiger reserve but poaching remains key threat
items.summary: JERANTUT: Despite encouraging signs that Malayan tigers are breeding in the country's first dedicated tiger reserve, conservationists say poaching and prey depletion remain the biggest threats to the species' long-term survival. Camera traps at the Al-Sultan Abdullah Royal Tiger Reserve (ASARTR) in Ulu Tembeling have recorded Malayan tiger cubs and juveniles, providing the strongest evidence yet that the critically endangered species is breeding in the protected area. The Habitat Foundation programme director Dr Ahmad Zafir Abdul Wahab said poaching and prey depletion remained the greatest threats to the reserve's tiger population.

items.title: Kidnapper of US TV host's mother apologised for her death
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: The alleged kidnapper of a US television star's mother apologised as he told her family six days after her disappearance that she had died, according to a note released by police. Nancy Guthrie, 84, vanished from her home in Arizona on the night of Jan 31-Feb 1, and her body has never been found. In a statement on Friday, six months after the kidnapping, the Pima County Sheriff's Department said the search for Guthrie was ongoing and asked for public assistance as it released two purported ransom notes sent to a local television station on Feb 2 and Feb 6.

items.title: Explosions in Kyiv, mayor says city 'under ballistic missile attack'
items.summary: KYIV, (Ukraine): Explosions were heard in Kyiv earlier today as the city's mayor said the Ukrainian capital was being attacked by ballistic missiles. Vitali Klitschko said. An AFP journalist also reported hearing explosions.

items.title: Negri Sembilan voters head to the polls today
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Voters in Negri Sembilan will fulfil their democratic rights and civic duty today in the 16th state election (PRN) to elect their new representatives. A total of 36 state legislative assembly (DUN) seats are being contested in the election, involving 103 candidates. The Negri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly was dissolved on June 5.

items.title: Lebanon president says Israeli blasts near castle 'direct threat' to recent deal
items.summary: BEIRUT: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun on Friday warned that Israeli detonations near a Unesco-listed castle threatened a recent deal with Israel, which in turn said it had razed Hizbollah tunnels there. Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported that "Israeli forces triggered very powerful explosions" overnight, specifically "in the area of the Beaufort fortress", a Crusader-era castle located near the southern border occupied by Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz said the army had destroyed "terror tunnels in the Beaufort area" using approximately 700 tonnes of explosives.

items.title: Negri Sembilan decides: Voters hold key to state's political future [WATCH]
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The political direction of Negri Sembilan hangs in the balance today as more than 850,000 eligible voters cast their ballots in a closely watched state election. Similar to the recent Johor polls, PH and BN are contesting against each other, with tensions in the state between the two coalitions intensifying after all 14 BN assemblymen withdrew their support for PH's Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun as menteri besar in April. However, unlike the Johor election, PH entered the contest as the caretaker state government, banking on its two-term record in administering Negri Sembilan and Aminuddin's track record as leader.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan votes today: 10 seats to watch in pivotal state election
items.summary: All 36 state seats are at stake, with the outcome carrying significance beyond Negeri Sembilan. Linggi (PH-PKR vs BN-Umno vs Bersatu) Linggi is expected to be one of the election’s defining contests after caretaker Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun left his long-held Sikamat seat to contest there. — Picture by Choo Choy May Pertang (BN-Umno vs PH-PKR vs Bersatu) Another closely watched contest is Pertang, where Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias is seeking re-election against PH’s Mohd Umry Abdul Khois and Bersatu’s Mohd Faizal Fadli Mohd Idrus.

items.title: Trump threatens to hit Iran 'very hard'
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump threatened on Friday to hit Iran "very hard", as US media reported he was considering renewed heavy attacks as soon as this weekend, including against energy infrastructure targets. *The Wall Street Journal* later reported that Trump had ordered a fresh attack aimed at convincing Teheran to surrender, which could begin as soon as this weekend, citing unnamed US officials. CBS News, meanwhile, reported that the United States and Israel were planning joint strikes on energy-related targets, possibly throughout the weekend.

items.title: Hundreds rally in Madrid against migrant 'invasion' in Ceuta
items.summary: MADRID: Hundreds of anti-migrant protesters rallied outside Morocco's embassy in Madrid on Friday evening to denounce what they called a migrant "invasion" of Spain's north African enclave of Ceuta. Several protesters performed Nazi salutes, some openly and without covering their faces. protesters chanted, many dressed entirely in black, an AFP journalist said.

items.title: US ICE detains Johns Hopkins researcher as airport arrests surge
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US immigration agents arrested a Johns Hopkins University researcher at an airport where she planned to board a domestic flight as immigration arrests by President Donald Trump's administration have surged at airports in recent weeks. Here are more details: Lawyers say there has been an uptick in immigration enforcement and arrests at airports. Fatima Ameaka, who is from Cameroon and an employee at the Bloomberg School of Public Health, was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at the Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said on Friday.

items.title: Figures behind rush for Hormuz oil export alternatives
items.summary: Of the remaining 13.26 mbd, as much as 11.5 mbd could eventually be rerouted by maximising existing pipeline capacity and completing planned projects, according to official announcements and industry experts. State oil giant Aramco said in March 2025 it had increased the pipeline's capacity to 7 mbd, leaving up to 5 mbd of spare capacity. The IEA said the pipeline had a capacity of 1.8 mbd, leaving an additional 0.7 mbd available.

items.title: At Farnborough airshow, tech and geopolitics drive aviation innovation
items.summary: ON the first day of the Farnborough airshow last week, an unusual-looking craft with upward-pointing propellers along its wings rose into the sky from the main runway: the new electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) lightweight "air taxi" from Britain's Vertical Aerospace. The Farnborough show and accompanying military and civilian aviation trade event have long showcased a mix of breakthroughs, breathlessly announced sales of existing aircraft types and a look into the future. Simultaneously, other new technology is leaping forward.

items.title: Preserve uniqueness of Kuching's old quarter
items.summary: A stone's throw away is the General Post Office, easily the most impressive of the city's old buildings with a colonnade of Corinthian columns spanning an entire city block. Speaking at the opening of another building transformed into a high-end hotel and elderly-care centre in Kuching this week, he pointed to another old post office building in Singapore which is now the Fullerton Hotel. The only problem is that the two-storey General Post Office building in Kuching is hemmed in with little space for an annex, unless the state government acquires the rows of shophouses behind the building.

items.title: Felda task force report to be released in coming months, says Anwar
items.summary: JEMPOL: The special task force report on the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) is expected to be completed within the next few months, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the report would be made public once it was finalised, in line with the government's commitment to transparency. "We have already released the Tabung Haji report.

items.title: NST Leader: Bumpy ride looms as telcos ride 5G wave
items.summary: FOR Malaysians, high-speed home broadband and 5G mobile subscriptions are either considered a divine right or a commodity. Household access to fixed high-speed broadband is at 97.1 per cent, or 50 subscriptions per 100 premises, covering 5.04 million homes and businesses. Mobile high-speed broadband topped 130.7 subscriptions per 100 inhabitants or 45 million accounts.

items.title: Man regrets missing sister's final video call before fatal crash
items.summary: GUA MUSANG: A man said the video call he missed from his sister last night turned out to be her last before she was killed in a crash involving a Perodua Myvi and a trailer at Km25 of Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Krai today. Maria's younger brother, Mohamad Faizol Yusoff, 34, said he received a video call from his sister at 9pm yesterday but did not answer it. He said he learnt about the tragedy involving his sister and nephew at 10am before rushing to Hospital Gua Musang.

items.title: TH moves to audited profits after RM1.4b loss discrepancy flagged by RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji's (TH) profit distribution is only announced based on audited financial results, thus strengthening the integrity of the financial reporting process and increasing depositors' confidence in the institution. The pilgrimage board said the RCI recommended that profit distributions be declared only based on audited financial statements, in line with the principles of good governance, transparency and financial sustainability. TH said that, according to the RCl report, TH's financial statements for the 2017 financial year did not fully adopt the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS).

items.title: Govt bears RM1.25b LPG subsidies for January-May
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has borne almost RM1.25 billion in liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) subsidies for the period from January to May 2026, said the Finance Ministry (MOF). The ministry said the government is adopting targeted subsidies for selected petroleum products to ease cost pressures and sustain key sectors amid a challenging geopolitical climate. "One of the products subsidised by the government at the moment is LPG," said MOF.

items.title: Police investigate viral videos of ketum juice sale at Paka R&R
items.summary: DUNGUN: Police have launched an investigation following two viral videos on social media allegedly showing the open sale of ketum juice at the exit of the Paka Rest and Recreation (R&R) area on the Kemaman-Kuala Terengganu route today. Dungun district police chief, Superintendent Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat, said initial investigations found that the incident was believed to have taken place during the RXZ Members 8.0 programme, with the location serving as a main route for participants travelling to the event venue. He said a team of police officers and personnel from the Dungun district police headquarters' Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division was immediately deployed to the location.

items.title: Malaysia records 2,001 factory fires, RM4.21b losses since 2020, says Fire Dept D-G
items.summary: To strengthen compliance with fire safety aspects, he said the JBPM continues to enhance industrial premises inspection activities. He said that a total of 1,878 factory premises were inspected in 2025 compared to 1,563 premises the previous year. “During the same period, the number of premises issued with Fire Hazard Elimination Notices (MBK) increased from 706 premises in 2024 to 1,191 premises in 2025,” he said.

items.title: EC reminds Negeri Sembilan voters to follow recommended times, phones barred during voting
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — The Election Commission (EC) has reminded voters in Negeri Sembilan to vote early or at their recommended voting times, while adhering to rules prohibiting mobile phone use and campaign materials at polling stations during tomorrow’s state election. However, they may vote anytime during polling hours from 8 am to 6 pm, depending on their polling centre’s operating hours. The EC said 15,344 polling officials will be responsible for conducting the voting process at 401 polling centres.

items.title: Police to investigate dog’s death during Klang stray‑catching operation, says Royal Klang City Council
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 31 — The Royal Klang City Council (MBDK) has handed over the investigation into an incident during a stray dog-catching operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah, Port Klang, which resulted in the death of a dog yesterday, to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM). MBDK said in a statement that the incident occurred during an operation conducted from 8.30pm to midnight following complaints from residents over safety concerns arising from an increase in the stray dog population. “The operation involved 11 personnel and an officer from the MBDK Health Department, together with about 50 local residents.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polls: Trustworthy leaders key to state’s future, Fahmi tells voters
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, July 31 — Voters should choose trustworthy leaders in tomorrow’s Negeri Sembilan state election to ensure the state continues to be governed effectively, Pakatan Harapan (PH) communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said every vote cast would help determine the state’s future direction, including ensuring public funds were managed prudently and development carried out for the people’s benefit. He said his observations during campaign visits to several constituencies showed growing enthusiasm among voters, with many Negeri Sembilan natives beginning to return home to cast their ballots.

items.title: Six surveys, six different results: Anwar tells Pakatan to focus on campaigning in Negeri Sembilan, not predictions
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Pakatan Harapan (PH) campaign machinery should utilise the remaining campaign period ahead of tomorrow’s Negeri Sembilan state election to continue working, rather than focusing too much on various election outcome predictions. Anwar, who is also PH chairman, said there are currently six surveys making predictions on the outcome of the state election, but their findings differ. “Six surveys, six different results.

items.title: Perlis Mufti wins partial defamation claim, awarded RM250,000 over GISBH posts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Perlis Mufti Datuk Mohd Asri Zainul Abidin was awarded RM250,000 in damages after the High Court ruled in his favour on part of his defamation claim against a Facebook account owner over posts linking him to GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH). Judicial Commissioner Rihaida Rafie allowed part of the suit filed by Mohd Asri, 55, against Mohd Nawawi Abdul Razak, 39. Today’s proceedings were attended by lawyers Faizal Rahman and Fatima Zulaikha Ahmad Bashri, representing Mohd Asri, while Mohd Nawawi was represented by Mohd Tajudin Abd Razak.

items.title: Malaysia, Singapore to jointly launch JS‑SEZ Master Plan in December, says Akmal Nasrullah
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, July 31 — The Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) Master Plan is expected to be officially launched in conjunction with the Annual Leaders’ Retreat this December, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said that the launch will be jointly conducted by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Singaporean counterpart Lawrence Wong, and is scheduled to take place in Malaysia. He said the launch of the master plan is expected to boost JS-SEZ’s position as a major regional investment destination.

items.title: Vessel carrying 41 undocumented migrants detained after ramming MMEA patrol boat four times
items.summary: IPOH, July 31 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) detained a vessel carrying 41 Indonesian undocumented migrants in the waters of Teluk Senangin near Batu Malang near Lumut early this morning. Perak MMEA director Capt (M) Mohamad Shukri Khotob said a MMEA patrol boat moved to the location to intercept the vessel following a public tipoff at 12.40 am. “The vessel also rammed the MMEA boat four times, which threatened the safety of the personnel,” he said in a statement today, adding that the MMEA personnel managed to block, intercept and detain the vessel at 3.35am.

items.title: CAAM to probe circumstances of Malaysian pilot’s detention in Indonesia over alleged drug smuggling attempt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) is investigating the reported detention of a Malaysian pilot in Indonesia from a regulatory perspective, including whether there were any lapses before the individual departed from Malaysia. CAAM said it is currently gathering the relevant facts regarding the reported incident involving the Malaysian pilot. As an immediate measure, CAAM said it will strengthen its oversight of existing regulatory requirements relating to baggage screening and security procedures, including those applicable to aircrew.

items.title: Anwar appeals to Tunisian president for release of opposition leader Ghannouchi on humanitarian grounds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has sent a letter to Tunisian President Kais Saied appealing for the release of political figure Sheikh Rached Ghannouchi on humanitarian grounds. Anwar said the appeal was made following his deep concern over the health condition of Ghannouchi, 84, whom he described as a friend and who remains in detention in Tunisia. “I have sent a letter to the President of the Republic of Tunisia, Kais Saied, requesting his due consideration of Ghannouchi’s health condition and advanced age, including the possibility of granting his release on compassionate and humanitarian grounds.

items.title: Seven‑hour closure on Batu Maung–Batu Kawan stretch of 2nd Penang Bridge on Aug 8 for Cultural Night Run
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 31 — The westbound carriageway of the Sultan Abdul Halim Mu’adzam Shah Bridge from Batu Maung to Batu Kawan will be temporarily closed for seven hours from 8pm on August 8 until 3am on August 9 in conjunction with the Cultural Night Run 2026. Jambatan Kedua Sdn Bhd (JKSB) said in a statement today that the closure would affect only the Batu Maung-to-Batu Kawan carriageway, while traffic from Batu Kawan to Batu Maung would continue to operate as usual throughout the period. Routes from Bandar Cassia, Batu Kawan and the Batu Kawan Industrial Park (BKIP) to the North-South Expressway (PLUS) would also remain open and accessible, it said.

items.title: Police confirm three fatalities, two injuries in multiple RXZ‑related motorcycle accidents across Pahang
items.summary: KUANTAN, July 31 — Three motorcyclists were killed and two others injured in four separate accidents in Pahang linked to the RXZ Members 8.0 gathering at the Gong Badak Motorsports Circuit in Kuala Nerus, Terengganu. Temerloh district police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police received information about the accident at 11pm, involving a Yamaha LC135 motorcycle rider who was travelling from Klang, Selangor, to Terengganu to attend the gathering. “The victim was believed to have lost control and fallen onto the left lane before being thrown onto the right lane.

items.title: PM pledges increased allocation for Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia in upcoming Budget to aid low‑income families
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 31 — The government will increase its allocation for Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia (AIM) in the upcoming Budget as part of its continued commitment to helping low-income families, particularly women, improve their economic well-being, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the government would enhance its support for AIM while maintaining the special allocation already provided to the agency. The prime minister also said the government would increase Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) assistance in the upcoming Budget.

items.title: High Court allows prosecution appeal, sets aside Papagomo’s acquittal in sedition case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — The High Court today set aside the sessions court’s acquittal of political influencer Wan Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, on a sedition charge and directed him to enter his defence. Justice Nurulhuda Nur’aini Nor delivered the ruling after allowing the prosecution’s appeal against the September 3, 2025 decision that freed Wan Azri without his defence being called, Free Malaysia Today reported. Wan Azri was also allowed bail of RM7,000.

items.title: Penang police bust Japan travel scam call centre in luxury condominium
items.summary: Northeast district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the Criminal Investigation Division of the Northeast district police headquarters (IPD) and Tanjung Tokong police station at 4.45 pm also arrested seven foreign men and a foreign woman aged between 25 and 37. Abdul Rozak said investigations found that the syndicate was offering travel packages to Japan online, targeting victims in China and Taiwan. He said the police would continue to intensify operations to combat criminal activities masterminded by foreigners, especially involving online fraud syndicates.

items.title: Senator files police report over video alleging DAP is a communist party, calls content ‘malicious and baseless’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — DAP senator Dr RA Lingeshwaran has filed a police report against a video circulating on social media that alleges the party is a communist organisation. “DAP is not a communist party and is not founded on any communist ideology,” Lingeshwaran said, stressing that the party is multiracial, upholds the Federal Constitution and supports Malaysia’s parliamentary system. Lingeshwaran argued the video was designed to provoke hatred, damage the party’s reputation and inflame racial tensions.

items.title: Malaysian Embassy seeks consular access to pilot arrested over 25kg Jakarta drug haul
items.summary: JAKARTA, July 31 — The Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta is seeking consular access to a Malaysian pilot detained in Indonesia on alleged drug trafficking offences following his arrest at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport earlier this week. The embassy said it had received official notification from Indonesia’s Directorate of Drug Crimes under the National Police Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) regarding the detention of the Malaysian national at Terminal 3 of the airport. “The Embassy respects Indonesia’s legal process and is engaging with the Indonesian authorities to obtain consular access to the Malaysian citizen concerned,” the embassy said in a statement on Friday.

items.title: Chong Chieng Jen files appeal against ‘black hole’ ruling permitting govt defamation suits, says decision against public interest
items.summary: KUCHING, July 31 — Sarawak Democratic Action Party (DAP) chairman Chong Chieng Jen has decided to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision against him in the ‘black hole’ case. “The Court of Appeal has, inter alia, decided that, in Malaysia, a government can sue its citizen for defamation. On July 3, the Court of Appeal here dismissed Chong’s appeal against the High Court’s ruling in the 2013 ‘black hole’ defamation suit and doubled the damages awarded.

items.title: ‘Let you die here’: Plumber gets eight years’ jail for attempted murder of 16‑year‑old girl in Penampang
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 31 — A plumber was sentenced to eight years in prison by the Sessions Court here for attempting to murder a teenage girl two months ago. The accused was charged with using a knife to stab the undocumented teenager, 16, in the neck inside a toilet of an unnumbered house in Penampang on May 7. The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor DK Afiqah Alya Ak Johari @ Pg Johari.

items.title: Johari urges investors to build with Malaysia, not simply sell to it
items.summary: TANJONG MALIM, July 31 — Foreign investments brought into Malaysia must deliver tangible benefits to the national economy, including helping to strengthen the trade surplus, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He noted that the country’s import value has reached RM1.45 trillion. It must grow.

items.title: Malaysia must accelerate charging infrastructure to drive EV adoption, minister says
items.summary: TANJONG MALIM, July 31 — The electric vehicle industry’s development should not focus solely on vehicle sales but must be supported by a comprehensive ecosystem, said Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. He said this ecosystem includes developing local technology, building a skilled workforce, and establishing an adequate network of public charging stations. Johari said that while hybrid technology is not new, Proton has managed to make it more affordable for the public.

items.title: UNHCR cards do not confer legal immigration status in Malaysia, department says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Holders of valid United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards are still regarded as illegal immigrants, but are exempted from prosecution under the Immigration Act 1959/63 for offences of overstaying and entering the country without valid travel documents, according to the Immigration Department (JIM). In a statement to Bernama today, the department said that apart from these exemptions, UNHCR cardholders remain subject to Malaysian laws. JIM also stressed that the public should not take matters into their own hands against foreign nationals, as doing so could have implications for security, public order and the law.

items.title: Anwar says Tabung Haji RCI report released in full, without redactions
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the full Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the management and operations of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) had been released in full without any censorship or redactions. The Prime Minister’s Department did not remove any part of the report. We published the entire report, including the recommendations and the processes that took place.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI report: Anwar questions 13-month bonus payout, calls it breach of trust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 31 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described the alleged payment of 13 months’ worth of bonuses to Tabung Haji staff despite the institution recording losses as a breach of trust. The issue was among several concerns raised in the Tabung Haji inquiry report, The Star reported today. He said such payments were among the many issues highlighted in the report, questioning how a loss-making institution could justify rewarding employees in such a manner.

items.title: Kuching High Court reduces Bau man’s jail term for sexually assaulting teen stepdaughter to 18 years
items.summary: This reduced the 54-year-old’s total imprisonment term from 54 years to 18 years. He was previously sentenced by the Kuching Sessions Court on October 31, 2025 to a total of 54 years’ imprisonment and 24 strokes of the cane. The Sessions Court imposed 18 years’ imprisonment for each of the three charges and ordered the sentences to run consecutively.

items.title: Warisan denies organising solidarity rally for Shafie Apdal in Kota Kinabalu, files police report over fake posters
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 31 — Parti Warisan (Warisan) has denied allegations it is organising a solidarity rally for president Datuk Seri Panglima Mohd Shafie Apdal at Padang Merdeka here on Sunday (August 2). Warisan secretary-general Loretto S. Padua Jr said the party has lodged a police report over the distribution of posters said to contain false information about the rally. Party members lodged the police report at the Kota Kinabalu Police Headquarters on Thursday evening.

items.title: Undecided voters and turnout take centre stage in Negeri Sembilan’s final campaign hours
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 31 — As the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election campaign enters its final hours, political coalitions and parties are intensifying their final campaign drive and strengthening their campaign operations ahead of tomorrow’s vote. Contesting parties have turned their attention to winning over undecided voters and boosting turnout before the campaign period officially ends at 11.59pm tonight. Negeri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said the coalition’s campaign machinery would continue its ground efforts ahead of polling, focusing especially on key areas identified as crucial.
